scope: Three current public/cultural destinations; performance, museum-session and cliff-maintenance constraints remain explicit field gates.

sources.supports: Dense current Aug–Dec 2026 event schedule, La Cultura station within 100 m and announced December maintenance period.
June 2026 registered accessible route through main hall, corridors, rehearsal rooms and backstage; not open access.
Current hours/program, accessible rooms/gardens, ordinary photo rules, tripod/session prohibition and professional authorization process.
Adapted eighteenth-century house and reuse of recovered railings, doors, columns, beams and corbels.
External public mirador/profile view of Larcomar's architecture and engineering at the cliff edge.
Current operation under 2026 surface-right agreement and scheduled 2026 cliff-slope maintenance/reinforcement; exact works state requires same-day check.

contradictions: A dense 2026 event calendar verifies active occupation but not audience density, exterior queue configuration or photography policy for a chosen performance.
Backstage and rehearsal spaces are accessible only through specific registered visits; public program evidence cannot authorize those positions.
composition_questions: Can the public terrace visibly transform transit arrivals into an audience before the façade becomes an isolated cultural icon?
Which barrier, vehicle, poster, column overlap or dense queue would sever station-origin, terrace and entrance destination?
Does moving to the oblique station-to-terrace path reveal civic gathering better than widening from a frontal plaza position?

source_truth.answer: Gran Teatro Nacional is an active national performing-arts venue at Javier Prado Este 2225, San Borja, with La Cultura station less than 100 m away.

original_spatial_contract.answer: An external public terrace, glazed foyer/performance volume and technical/backstage system separate civic arrival, audience preparation and production work while keeping them connected.

current_life.answer: The official calendar verifies continuous 2026 music, dance, opera, rehearsal/montage and public programming, followed by an announced December maintenance period.

human_verbs_or_meaningful_absence.answer: Arrive, cross, queue, wait, enter, rehearse, guide and perform are evidenced. The public scene should link station-to-terrace arrival with waiting and entry.

architectural_causality.answer: Terrace, broad approach, transparent foyer and controlled doors collect dispersed transit arrivals and convert them into staged audience movement.

visual_forensic_saturation.answer: Frontal glazed-façade overviews, empty night architecture and stage imagery dominate. The underused frame treats the terrace as transit-to-culture infrastructure at human scale.

light_material_geometry.answer: Blue-hour balance can reveal glass, interior audience light and exterior terrace depth; daylight side light can separate approach planes without signage dominating.

position_then_optics.answer: Test lawful station-side approach, terrace edge and oblique entrance line. Start 50 mm for arrival/wait/entry, 35 mm for full transit section and 85 mm from distance for layered figures against foyer.

moment_logistics_ethics.answer: Choose a verified event, arrive 30 minutes before doors, stay outside security/queue lines, avoid identifiable children and use backstage only through registered permission.

one_frame_contest_test.answer: The frame passes when architecture visibly turns urban transit into collective cultural arrival. A façade portrait, random queue or performance image fails.

contradictions: Current rules allow non-professional photography but prohibit photo sessions and tripods; professional work requires museum authorization at least three business days ahead.
Official garden imagery cannot verify current bloom, quiet conditions or whether salvaged architectural fragments read in one frame.
composition_questions: Can a visitor's route reveal how recovered architectural fragments and an adapted house produce a contemporary museum rather than a picturesque colonial backdrop?
Which bougainvillea mass, café table, display sign or visitor overlap would hide the transition between garden, threshold and collection route?
Does moving from postcard courtyard center to a fragment/doorway junction reveal adaptation more clearly than changing focal length?

source_truth.answer: Museo Larco operates in an adapted eighteenth-century Pueblo Libre house whose fabric incorporates recovered railings, doors, columns, beams and corbels.

original_spatial_contract.answer: Domestic courtyards, rooms and gardens were reassembled/adapted to receive collection display and visitor circulation, making fragments part of a new institutional whole.

current_life.answer: The museum currently operates rooms, visible storage, gardens, café and mediated activities; access and photography follow explicit current rules.

human_verbs_or_meaningful_absence.answer: Enter, cross, look, compare, pause, learn and dine are current. The decisive verb is a visitor moving from planted courtyard through a recovered threshold into collection space.

architectural_causality.answer: Courtyards, gardens, reused doors/columns and room thresholds pace movement from exterior relief to concentrated viewing.

visual_forensic_saturation.answer: Bougainvillea/white-wall postcards, empty courtyard views and artifact close-ups dominate. The underused frame links a specific salvaged element to present visitor transition.

light_material_geometry.answer: Soft courtyard light can separate vegetation, white walls and dark reused timber/metal; hard midday contrast may erase the fragment/whole relation.

position_then_optics.answer: With permission test garden-to-door junction, oblique courtyard edge and room threshold. Start 50 mm for visitor/fragment, 35 mm for garden-house depth and 85 mm from a lawful distance for layered material transition.

moment_logistics_ethics.answer: Request professional authorization in advance, use no tripod/flash, do not stage a session or obstruct visitors, protect minors and leave if the intended workflow is not approved.

one_frame_contest_test.answer: The frame passes when a reused architectural element visibly channels contemporary discovery. A floral postcard, artifact portrait or café lifestyle image fails.

A_STRUCTURE.position: Authorized oblique courtyard edge aligning garden, reused threshold and interior room
A_STRUCTURE.edge_guards: Control flowers, café furniture and bright walls

B_HABITAR.expected_action: Visitor pauses at fragment then enters gallery
B_HABITAR.edge_guards: Separate person, reused element and destination

C_ANTI_POSTAL.position: Low side angle behind one recovered element, away from central flower view
C_ANTI_POSTAL.expected_action: Figure moves between fragment and adapted room
C_ANTI_POSTAL.edge_guards: No centered bougainvillea or café scene

D_LIGHT_MATERIAL.position: Authorized distant line across timber/metal fragment and white wall depth
D_LIGHT_MATERIAL.expected_action: Hand or shadow crosses material seam

E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.position: Authorized oblique route combining garden pause, recovered doorway and gallery entry
E_ONE_FRAME_STORY.edge_guards: No floral mass or object display dominates

contradictions: The 2026 agreement confirms operation but also schedules cliff-slope maintenance/reinforcement, so access, sightlines and edge condition must be checked on the visit date.
Historical temporary closure evidence cannot be treated as a current defect, and operator activity cannot prove every mirador/terrace is open.
composition_questions: Can one frame show the cliff excavation simultaneously carrying park-level walking and suspended commercial occupation without becoming a sunset panorama?
Which railing, sign, planter, construction barrier or horizon overlap would flatten the vertical section?
Does moving to an external mirador or lower oblique profile reveal excavation/occupation better than widening from inside the mall?

source_truth.answer: Larcomar operates beneath/within Parque Salazar's cliff-top land under a current municipal surface-right agreement covering park, cliff and subsurface.

original_spatial_contract.answer: The complex excavates rather than crowns the cliff, stacking park-level public movement, void-facing commercial rooms and coastal outlook in a vertical section.

current_life.answer: The commercial complex remains operating in 2026, while the agreement requires same-year cliff maintenance/reinforcement and ornamental recovery at Parque Salazar.

human_verbs_or_meaningful_absence.answer: Walk, overlook, descend, shop, dine, wait and photograph are credible. The decisive relation layers a park walker above a descending/void-facing occupant below.

architectural_causality.answer: Excavated terraces, stairs, retaining edges and suspended rooms convert topographic drop into separated but visually connected movement levels.

visual_forensic_saturation.answer: Sunset/ocean panoramas, tourist overlooks and mall interiors dominate. The underused frame uses an external profile to show park, cliff engineering and occupied void together.

light_material_geometry.answer: Garúa can simplify sea/sky and reveal retaining planes; late side light can articulate excavation depth but must not reduce the image to sunset atmosphere.

position_then_optics.answer: Verify external Mirador-2/profile, park-level edge and lawful internal descent. Start 50 mm for two-level occupation, 35 mm for complete section and 85 mm from external distance for stacked park/cliff/room layers.

moment_logistics_ethics.answer: Check same-day works and closures, never cross barriers or stop on unsafe lower roads, avoid identifiable children and abandon any profile whose safe public position is unavailable.

one_frame_contest_test.answer: The frame passes when occupied architecture visibly negotiates public park and unstable cliff section. A sunset, shopping or ocean-view image fails.

A_STRUCTURE.edge_guards: Exclude dominant horizon, railings and works barriers
